14:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκόν τινος τῶν ἀρχόντων τῶν Φαρισαίων σαββάτῳ φαγεῖν ἄρτον, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦσαν παρατηρούμενοι αὐτόν.
14:1.targetText: And it came to pass, on His going into the house of a certain one of the chiefs of the Pharisees, on a Sabbath, to eat bread, that they were watching Him,

groups.note: Actual accusative αὐτόν is the personal subject of the articular going infinitive, rendered His in the nominal temporal phrase. No genitive Greek possessive form is substituted.
Actual καί introduces the main they-were-watching clause under the came-to-pass temporal frame. English realizes that same clause connection as that; no Greek ὅτι form is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

14:2.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν ὑδρωπικὸς ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ.
14:2.targetText: and behold, there was a certain dropsical man before Him;

14:3.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς νομικοὺς καὶ Φαρισαίους λέγων Ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεῦσαι ἢ οὔ;
14:3.targetText: and Jesus answering spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Pinned N1904 explicitly ends the lawful-healing question with or not. LSV states the shorter positive-form question without separately rendering that negative alternative.

14:4.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἡσύχασαν. καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος ἰάσατο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπέλυσεν.
14:4.targetText: And they were silent, and having taken hold of [him], He healed him, and let [him] go;

groups.note: The actual man-object αὐτόν of healed is shared by the immediately coordinated taking-hold and letting-go actions. English repeats that same patient as two bracketed [him] objects; no additional Greek pronouns or different patients are invented.

14:5.sourceText: καὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν Τίνος ὑμῶν υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς εἰς φρέαρ πεσεῖται, καὶ οὐκ εὐθέως ἀνασπάσει αὐτὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;
14:5.targetText: and answering them He said, “Of which of you will a donkey or ox fall into a pit, and he will not immediately draw it up on the Sabbath day?”

groups.note: Actual πρὸς αὐτούς is the to-them saying-recipient phrase. English renders those same addressed people as the unprepositional recipient them beside its added answering wording; no answering verb is claimed for the source preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 names a son as the first pit-falling alternative, while LSV names a donkey. The unlike human/animal lexical heads are kept explicit, not treated as interchangeable.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness includes an answering participle; pinned N1904 has and/to-them/said without this separate response predicate.
LSV names a donkey in the first alternative, whereas pinned N1904 has a son. No Greek donkey lemma is invented for the actual υἱός son word.

14:6.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἀνταποκριθῆναι πρὸς ταῦτα.
14:6.targetText: And they were not able to answer Him again to these things.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness explicitly supplies the answering recipient Him. Pinned N1904 has the answer-back predicate and to-these-things content phrase, without a separately written personal recipient here.

14:7.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς κεκλημένους παραβολήν, ἐπέχων πῶς τὰς πρωτοκλισίας ἐξελέγοντο, λέγων πρὸς αὐτούς
14:7.targetText: And He spoke an allegory to those called, marking how they were choosing out the first couches, saying to them,

groups.note: Actual ἐπέχων is the attending/noticing predicate, rendered marking in the observe/notice sense. No Greek writing/inscribing head is claimed.

14:8.sourceText: Ὅταν κληθῇς ὑπό τινος εἰς γάμους, μὴ κατακλιθῇς εἰς τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν, μή ποτε ἐντιμότερός σου ᾖ κεκλημένος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ,
14:8.targetText: “When you may be called by anyone to wedding feasts, you may not recline on the first couch, lest [one] more honorable than you may have been called by him,

groups.note: Actual substantival comparative adjective names the more-honored person. English [one] realizes that same personal adjective phrase without an independent Greek one/person noun.

14:9.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ σὲ καὶ αὐτὸν καλέσας ἐρεῖ σοι Δὸς τούτῳ τόπον, καὶ τότε ἄρξῃ μετὰ αἰσχύνης τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον κατέχειν.
14:9.targetText: and he who called you and him having come will say to you, Give to this one [your] place, and then you may begin to occupy the last place with shame.

groups.note: Pinned N1904 morphology analyzes actual ἄρξῃ as future middle indicative, while LSV renders you may begin. The same written Greek form can receive a subjunctive analysis in another parsing tradition; this is an analysis ambiguity, not a claimed different-spelling source witness.

unmappedTarget.reason: English states the giving person’s understood place as [your] place. Pinned N1904 prints a place object without a separately written personal possessive here; the understood seat allocation is not denied.

14:10.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ὅταν κληθῇς, πορευθεὶς ἀνάπεσε εἰς τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον, ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ κεκληκώς σε ἐρεῖ σοι Φίλε, προσανάβηθι ἀνώτερον· τότε ἔσται σοι δόξα ἐνώπιον πάντων τῶν συνανακειμένων σοι.
14:10.targetText: But when you may be called, having gone on, recline in the last place, that when he who called you may come, he may say to you, Friend, come up higher; then you will have glory before those dining with you;

groups.note: Actual ἐρεῖ is future active indicative in pinned N1904, whereas LSV he may say follows the subjunctive wording represented by TR εἴπῃ. The shared saying predicate is linked while the actual future source form and witness difference remain explicit.
Actual ἔσται σοι is the there-will-be-to-you possession/benefit construction, rendered you will have. No Greek have verb or nominative source you pronoun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 explicitly says all the co-diners. LSV says those dining with you without a separately rendered all extent word.

14:11.sourceText: ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ὁ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
14:11.targetText: because everyone who is exalting himself will be humbled, and he who is humbling himself will be exalted.”

14:12.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μή ποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε καὶ γένηται ἀνταπόδομά σοι.
14:12.targetText: And He also said to him who called Him, “When you may make an early meal or a dinner, do not be calling your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor rich neighbors, lest they may also call you again, and a repayment may come to you;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

14:13.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ὅταν δοχὴν ποιῇς, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπήρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς·
14:13.targetText: but when you may make a feast, be calling poor, maimed, lame, blind,

14:14.sourceText: καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι· ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.
14:14.targetText: and you will be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you, for it will be repaid to you in the resurrection of the righteous.”

groups.note: Actual οὐκ ἔχουσιν is the negative they-do-not-have construction with the following repayment infinitive. English recasts the same lack of repayment means as they have nothing; no independent Greek nothing noun is claimed.

14:15.sourceText: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μακάριος ὅστις φάγεται ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
14:15.targetText: And one of those dining with Him, having heard these things, said to Him, “Blessed [is] he who will eat bread in the Kingdom of God”;

unmappedTarget.reason: English identifies the dining company as with Him. Pinned N1904 prints the co-dining participle without a separately written personal company pronoun here; no extra αὐτῷ form is claimed.
English supplies the present copula in the nominal blessed saying; actual μακάριος is an adjective, not a written be verb.

14:16.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς,
14:16.targetText: and He said to him, “A certain man made a great dinner, and called many,

14:17.sourceText: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις Ἔρχεσθε, ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ἐστιν.
14:17.targetText: and he sent his servant at the hour of the dinner to say to those having been called, Be coming, because now all things are ready.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness explicitly includes πάντα all things. Pinned N1904 has the plural ready predicate and its copula without that separately printed totalizing subject phrase.

14:18.sourceText: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι. ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα, καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.
14:18.targetText: And all began with one [voice] to excuse themselves. The first said to him, I bought a field, and I have need to go forth and see it; I beg of you, have me excused.

groups.note: Actual ἀπὸ μιᾶς is the elliptical from-one/unanimously expression. English renders its united-response scope as with one; the bracketed voice noun is separately identified as unwritten, not attributed to a Greek φωνή lemma.
Actual middle παραιτεῖσθαι supplies the excusing-oneself/refusal predicate. English themselves realizes the same middle action, without a separate source reflexive pronoun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies voice to complete the Greek elliptical from-one expression; pinned N1904 prints no voice noun in this phrase.

14:19.sourceText: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε, καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.
14:19.targetText: And another said, I bought five yoke of oxen, and I go on to prove them; I beg of you, have me excused.

14:20.sourceText: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν Γυναῖκα ἔγημα, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν.
14:20.targetText: And another said, I married a wife, and because of this I am not able to come.

14:21.sourceText: καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα. τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως, καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπήρους καὶ τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς εἰσάγαγε ὧδε.
14:21.targetText: And that servant having come, told these things to his lord, then the master of the house, having been angry, said to his servant, Go forth quickly into the broad places and lanes of the city, and the poor, and maimed, and lame, and blind, bring in here.

14:22.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος Κύριε, γέγονεν ὃ ἐπέταξας, καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν.
14:22.targetText: And the servant said, Lord, it has been done as you commanded, and still there is room.

groups.note: Actual relative ὃ introduces what was commanded and has come to pass. English joins that same command/result relation with as; no separate manner adverb is claimed for the written relative pronoun.

14:23.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν, ἵνα γεμισθῇ μου ὁ οἶκος·
14:23.targetText: And the lord said to the servant, Go forth into the ways and hedges, and constrain to come in, that my house may be filled;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

14:24.sourceText: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ δείπνου.
14:24.targetText: for I say to you that none of those men who have been called will taste of my dinner.”

14:25.sourceText: Συνεπορεύοντο δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς
14:25.targetText: And there were going on with Him great multitudes, and having turned, He said to them,

14:26.sourceText: Εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρός με καὶ οὐ μισεῖ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τὰς ἀδελφάς, ἔτι τε καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἑαυτοῦ, οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.
14:26.targetText: “If anyone comes to Me, and does not hate his own father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and yet even his own life, he is not able to be My disciple;

groups.note: Actual αὐτοῦ is the third-person possessor of the father phrase. English states that same ownership as his own; the source remains αὐτοῦ, not a substituted written reflexive ἑαυτοῦ form.

14:27.sourceText: ὅστις οὐ βαστάζει τὸν σταυρὸν ἑαυτοῦ καὶ ἔρχεται ὀπίσω μου, οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.
14:27.targetText: and whoever does not carry his cross, and come after Me, is not able to be My disciple.

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly connects this sentence with and. Pinned N1904 begins with whoever, without a separately written initial conjunction here.

14:28.sourceText: Τίς γὰρ ἐξ ὑμῶν θέλων πύργον οἰκοδομῆσαι οὐχὶ πρῶτον καθίσας ψηφίζει τὴν δαπάνην, εἰ ἔχει εἰς ἀπαρτισμόν;
14:28.targetText: For who of you, willing to build a tower, does not first, having sat down, count the expense, whether he has the things for completing?

unmappedTarget.reason: English states the implied means as the things for completing. Pinned N1904 prints has and the for-completion purpose phrase without a separately written things noun or article object here.

14:29.sourceText: ἵνα μή ποτε θέντος αὐτοῦ θεμέλιον καὶ μὴ ἰσχύοντος ἐκτελέσαι πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντες ἄρξωνται αὐτῷ ἐμπαίζειν
14:29.targetText: Lest that he having laid a foundation, and not being able to finish, all who are beholding may begin to mock him,

groups.note: Actual genitive αὐτοῦ is the personal subject of the laid-foundation genitive-absolute construction. English expresses that same person as he in its finite-style frame; no Greek nominative form is substituted.

14:30.sourceText: λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἤρξατο οἰκοδομεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἐκτελέσαι.
14:30.targetText: saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ὅτι introduces the quoted this-man statement. English uses direct quoted speech without a separately rendered that quotation marker.

14:31.sourceText: Ἢ τίς βασιλεὺς πορευόμενος ἑτέρῳ βασιλεῖ συμβαλεῖν εἰς πόλεμον οὐχὶ καθίσας πρῶτον βουλεύσεται εἰ δυνατός ἐστιν ἐν δέκα χιλιάσιν ὑπαντῆσαι τῷ μετὰ εἴκοσι χιλιάδων ἐρχομένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτόν;
14:31.targetText: Or what king going on to engage with another king in war, does not, having sat down, first consult if he with ten thousand is able to meet him who is coming against him with twenty thousand?

groups.note: Actual βουλεύσεται is a future deliberating/consulting predicate. English states the same deliberation in the present-form does-consult question; no present-tense Greek form is invented.

14:32.sourceText: εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἔτι αὐτοῦ πόρρω ὄντος πρεσβείαν ἀποστείλας ἐρωτᾷ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην.
14:32.targetText: And if not so—he being yet a long way off—having sent a delegation, he asks the things for peace.

groups.note: Actual genitive αὐτοῦ belongs to the being-far-away genitive absolute. English gives that same still-distant person as he; no nominative source pronoun is claimed.

14:33.sourceText: οὕτως οὖν πᾶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ὃς οὐκ ἀποτάσσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὑπάρχουσιν οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.
14:33.targetText: So, then, everyone of you who does not take leave of all that he himself has, is not able to be My disciple.

groups.note: Actual articular τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὑπάρχουσιν is the nominal construction for the things belonging to that same person. English recasts those possessions as that he himself has; no Greek ἔχω verb or independent nominative he is invented.

14:34.sourceText: Καλὸν οὖν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἀρτυθήσεται;
14:34.targetText: The salt [is] good, but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?

groups.note: Actual μωρανθῇ is the passive-subjunctive become-foolish/lose-flavor predicate in the salt clause. English renders the same loss-of-flavor predicate as becomes tasteless; no separate taste adjective or active Greek form is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual οὖν marks an inferential therefore connection; English does not separately state that inferential connector here.
Actual καί adds even/also emphasis within the if-the-salt clause; English states the condition without a separate emphatic word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula for the nominal good-salt predicate. Actual καλόν is an adjective, not a printed be verb.

14:35.sourceText: οὔτε εἰς γῆν οὔτε εἰς κοπρίαν εὔθετόν ἐστιν· ἔξω βάλλουσιν αὐτό. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
14:35.targetText: It is neither fit for land nor for manure—they cast it outside. He who is having ears to hear—let him hear.”
